notes: SHIP v1.14.377 - OPS WALL RE-CUT AT 768, FROM ART-DROP-SHIP-379. Owner: reuse ops-optics for the tools card, ship it. This ships the OPS HALF of the drop only; the TOOLS half is deliberately held and the reason is stated below, not glossed. THE DROP ITSELF WAS THE GOOD ONE: ART-DROP-SHIP-379 supersedes 377 and 378 in full, is structured as OODA, and explicitly instructs that the repo overrules the doc wherever they disagree. It had already absorbed every objection raised against 378 - the nine-cell wall list including OPTICS and AUDITS, files-not-inline, repo naming, PRECACHE entries, the 1:1-into-wide-cell aspect problem, and sequencing behind the unpushed inventory-tool commits. O2 PRECACHE_URLS was 54. O3 the wall is NINE cells, confirmed from the live per-cell --tim tokens, not from the doc. O4 IS THE HEADLINE AND IT CONTRADICTS THE DOC'S CENTRAL DEFERRAL: .opswall > div carries aspect-ratio:1/1 and the grid is repeat(3,1fr) with NO media query altering it, so OPS cells are SQUARE on every shell - 118px phone, 241px at 640, 348px at 980. A 768 square asset is therefore an exact aspect match at every width and still covers 2x retina at desktop, so R4's deferral of desktop OPS wiring was unnecessary and no desktop strip recut is needed for the wall. My own memory said this cell was 3.95:1 at 348x88; that was true at .366 and the .359-to-.372 rework changed it - measured, not recalled. R4 DOES still hold for TOOLS, whose .rf-grid-wrap is 2 columns then 3 at 640 then 4 at 980 with .rf-card min-height 124px, roughly 1.4:1 on phone widening to about 2:1 on desktop. O5/O6 the real TOOLS grid is seven .rf-cards - OPTICS, PLATFORMS, CLI, PARTS, KNOW, COMPASS, GHOST ECHO. PLATFORMS exists; PORT MAP DOES NOT, so per the doc's own O5 rule it is out of scope for TOOLS. Building that layout from the written spec alone would be adapting an approved visual rather than executing it, which is the one thing EXECUTE-DONT-ADAPT forbids. Needs the mock, or an explicit owner ruling to proceed from D5's text.
